summary: This class explores traditional customs of Hanukat Habayit, including the meal served to guests so they will bless the new home. It discusses the custom mentioned in Keter Shem Tob of bringing chickens, flour, and olive oil into a home before shehita as a kapara and sedaka for aniyim. The class also describes how shehita of a lamb was done for a new home in Brooklyn in 1930 and customs still observed today.
questions: Why is a full meal served to guests at a Hanukat Habayit?
How does the speaker connect serving food at a Hanukat Habayit to Yishak Abinu?
What custom does Keter Shem Tob describe regarding chickens, olive oil, and flour in Syria?
Was shehita ever done for a new home in Brooklyn?
Where is the custom of shehita for a new home still observed today?
